body.p: The Examiner's Office Action has been reviewed. Claim Rejection 35 USC X101

In response to the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 and section 33(a) of the America Invents Act as being directed to or encompassing a human organism, the limitation requiring a user having an amputated limb has been removed. Claim Rejection 35 USC 103

In response to the rejection of Claims 1-3 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over US 2017/0105853 Al to Jonsson in view of US 2017/0162153 Al to Barnes, the claims have been amended to more precisely claim that the measuring template is separate and distinct from the tapered sock, which is supported by the disclosure. See Disclosure at Figs. 4, 6; see also [0025] ("the measuring template 26 is put in place against the outer surface 34 of the prosthetic sock 10") (emphasis added). The zero mark on the separate measuring template creates the baseline mark on the sock which then moves up or down based on swelling or shrinkage of an amputated limb. The lines cited by the Examiner in Jonsson, on the other hand, are part and parcel with the sock. Specifically, the elements cited by the Examiner, elements 252 and 254, are removable sealing rings or seal bands that become physically part of the sock when put in place. See Jonsson at Fig. 25. Furthermore, the sealing rings or seal bands of Jonsson are made specifically to prevent upward or downward shifts due to swelling or shrinkage. See Jonsson at [0010] ("Some users find that known liners having sealing means fail to sufficiently tolerate volume fluctuations."); see also id. at [0159] ("the seal-in suspension can stabilize volume of the residual limb") and [0186] ("The seal height may be decided according to the user's needs, and the seal may be moved to adapt to various volume changes of the residual limb."). Likewise, Barnes does not teach a separate measuring template system and is solely relied on for the tapered sock limitations.
Based on these amendments, it is respectfully urged that this rejection has been overcome and the application is in condition for allowance.

It is urged that the application is now in condition for allowance. Should the Examiner have additional issues or suggested amendments, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at: 813-445-5175 to expedite allowance of this application.
